subject: Ask: Inference pathway-level cost & latency matrix for Console home
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ask: Inference pathway-level cost & latency matrix for Console home

Team —

Quick ask to get aligned before the product sync: a number of customers (Acme included) are asking for a single Console tile that surfaces per-inference-pathway economics and tail-latency risk. By "pathway" I mean the end-to-end API route (customer route + invoked tools/model variant) aggregated into a single time-window. Main goals: make hotspots visible on the Console home, enable a 1-click drill into per-tenant slices, and offer a suggested action (e.g., enable prefix caching, swap to quantized variant, or set a sampling-rate).

What I'd like to surface in the minimum viable tile: 
- Pathway name / canonical route id
- 24h cost ($) and tokens
- Avg latency / p95 tail latency (95th/99th)
- Request throughput (rps) and spike indicator
- A short signal: "cost per token" vs baseline and suggested knob (cache/batch/quantize)

I attached a small sample CSV from Acme that shows a few pathways and an example mockup image. Can we get a proposal on feasibility, required instrumentation changes, and ETA for a first-pass (Console home + drill to route inspector) by EOD Friday? If we can't hit Friday, please propose the earliest realistic milestone.

Notes / constraints I already know: we should avoid increasing high-cardinality telemetry on the hot path; prefer a sampled enrichment approach with deterministic sampling keys for reproducibility. Also need to list the data retention windows where metrics will be available.

Thanks — Mike

--
Michael Grant
Product Lead, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ask: Inference pathway-level cost & latency matrix for Console home

Mike —

Thanks for the concrete ask and the sample. Initial thoughts/questions:

1) Scope: do you want the tile to show live (near-real-time) metrics or daily rollups? Live would need a streaming aggregation path; daily rollups could reuse jobs we already run.
2) Drill path: when the user clicks a pathway, should the drill show raw traces (trace IDs) or a summarized slice (top callers, top prompt tokens, exemplar requests)?
3) Suggested action list: are we ok starting with a limited set of suggested items (cache, downgrading to a cheaper variant, and sampling) and expanding later?

I can do an initial feasibility write-up and a rough mockup for Friday if Soojin/infra confirms the telemetry cost. For ETA: if we have to add sampled enrichment at ingest, I think a phased plan (mock + nightly rollup in 3 weeks, near-RT in 8-10 weeks) is realistic.

Linking the Drive spec here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-matrix-spec

—Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ask: Inference pathway-level cost & latency matrix for Console home

Thanks Mike / Marissa —

Quick technical constraints from instrumentation/runtime:
- We can surface daily rollups without changing the hot path: existing batch jobs can join token-count and latency histograms keyed by (route_id, model_variant, customer_id). That supports the Console tile and the drill to aggregated tenant slices.
- Near-RT/streaming: will require adding a lightweight enrichment at the edge to tag a deterministic sample id. Doing full high-cardinality joins in the stream is expensive; we should cap cardinality by hashing to a fixed number of "pathway buckets" for intermediates.
- Tail latency (p95/p99): we currently store sketches for latency per-tenant at 1h buckets; to get pathway-level tail we need to ensure model_variant is retained in the sketch key or compute a cross-product in nightly jobs (can be heavy).

Risks & tradeoffs:
- If we leave everything to nightly rollups, the tile won't help with operational incidents that need minute-level visibility.
- If we do near-RT with bucketed pathways, we reduce cardinality but may miss fine-grained tenant-specific tails (we can fall back to a historical drill).

Proposed phased delivery:
1) Week 1 (spec + mock): product & UX mock plus schema for nightly rollup (no infra changes).
2) Week 3 (nightly rollup): Console tile + drill to aggregated tenant slices using existing batch pipelines.
3) Week 9 (streaming MVP): sampled enrichment + bucketed pathway streaming aggregates for near-RT surface and an opt-in per-tenant higher-cardinality mode behind a feature flag.

I'll coordinate with infra to estimate compute + storage delta once PMs confirm scope (live vs daily).

Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ask: Inference pathway-level cost & latency matrix for Console home

All —

I talked to infra briefly. Action items I can pick up:
- Pull a 7-day sample from prod for the provided Acme CSV and run a quick aggregation to validate the nightly rollup numbers (I expect this to be done by Wed EOD).
- Put together a short bullet estimating O(GB) storage delta for nightly rollups and O(% CPU) estimate for the streaming enrichment prototype if we go that route.

Agree with Soojin on phased approach. Marissa — if you can confirm we start with daily rollups and three suggested actions (cache/bump-quantize/sampling), I'll proceed with the sample run and a one-pager for exec review.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
